Daily notes on machine translation

Models that read whole sentences at once changed the field.

Before transformers, most sequence models processed tokens one at a time, which made training slow and long-range dependencies hard to learn. Attention lets every token look at every other token in a single step.

Jump up to: Attention weights come from queries and keys, scaled by the square root of the key size and normalised with a softmax.

Layer normalisation keeps the activations in a stable range. It is applied before or after each sub-layer, and the choice changes how deep a model can be trained without warm-up. Residual connections carry the input of each sub-layer around it, so gradients reach the early layers directly. Dropout on the attention weights and on the outputs of each sub-layer regularises the model while it trains.

Multi-head self-attention runs several attention operations in parallel and joins their results.

Positional encodings inject information about the order of the tokens into the model.
